\section{The published results formalised in the archive}\label{app:rows}

One row for each of the \literaturerows{} theorems of the archive's literature file (\cref{sec:literature}), in the order of the file. The second column says what the Lean statement asserts, in our words; where the statement is a conjunction of named parts the description covers the parts. After it, in italics, is our comparison with the published theorem that the name refers to, and the third column gives its outcome: \emph{general}, the published theorem in the generality of a cited source; \emph{restricted}, a special case of it or a weaker form; \emph{differs}, not a statement of the cited literature as it stands. The other labels are internal (a statement in the archive's own terms), empty, conclusion and repeated. The comparison was made from the Lean statement and from our knowledge of the published theorem; we did not open the papers for it, and a row should be checked against its sources before it is relied on. The fourth column gives the sources, from the reference research.

\leanb{Log\allowbreak{}Der\allowbreak{}One} & There is $C$ such that $\bigl|\tfrac{L'}{L}(1,\chi)-\sum_\rho\tfrac1{1-\rho}\bigr|\le C\log 3q$ for every primitive $\chi$ modulo $q>1$, the sum over the zeros with $0<\re\rho<1$ and $\abs{\im\rho}\le1$. \emph{The value at $s=1$ of the classical formula for $L'/L$ in terms of nearby zeros.} & restricted & \cite{davenport1980multiplicative}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Elliptic\allowbreak{}Main\allowbreak{}Theorem\allowbreak{}CM} & The main theorem of complex multiplication for elliptic curves with CM by an imaginary quadratic field $K$, in idelic form: if $\sigma\in\mathrm{Aut}(\C/K)$ restricts to $\mathrm{Art}(s)$, then $\sigma$ transports an analytic uniformisation $\C/\mathfrak a\to E(\C)$ according to the finite part of $s$. \emph{Imaginary quadratic fields and lattices that are fractional ideals of the maximal order; Shimura's theorem covers any lattice and CM abelian varieties.} & restricted & \cite{shimura1971introduction,shimura1961complex}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hecke\allowbreak{}Tate\allowbreak{}Functional\allowbreak{}Equation} & For a unitary Hecke character $\chi$ of a totally complex field with non-zero infinity type relative to a CM type, the completed $L$-functions of $\chi$ and $\chi^{-1}$ exist and $\Lambda(s,\chi)=\varepsilon_\infty\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm f}(s)\,\Lambda(1-s,\chi^{-1})$. \emph{Totally complex fields and infinity types coming from a CM type; the published theorem covers every Hecke character of every number field.} & restricted & \cite{hecke1918neue,hecke1920neue,tate1967fourier}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hilbert\allowbreak{}Class\allowbreak{}Field\allowbreak{}J} & For $K$ imaginary quadratic, $K(j(\cO_K))$ is the Hilbert class field, of degree $h_K$; $j(\mathfrak a)=j(\mathfrak b)$ exactly when the ideal classes agree; and the $h_K$ values $j(\mathfrak a)$ are the conjugates of $j(\cO_K)$ over $K$. \emph{The first main theorem of complex multiplication for the maximal order.} & general & \cite{hasse1927neue,shimura1971introduction}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Partial\allowbreak{}Zeta\allowbreak{}Functional\allowbreak{}Equation} & For $F$ totally real of degree $n$ and ideal classes $C,C'$ whose product is the class of the different: $d_F^{s/2}\Gamma_\R(s)^n\zeta(s,C)=d_F^{(1-s)/2}\Gamma_\R(1-s)^n\zeta(1-s,C')$. \emph{Totally real fields; Hecke's functional equation holds for every number field.} & restricted & \cite{hecke1917zetafunktion,tate1967fourier}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Deligne\allowbreak{}Ribet} & For $F$ totally real and a $\Q$-valued function $\varepsilon$ on ideals that is constant on narrow ray classes modulo $\ell^n$ and $\ell$-integral: $L(1-k,\varepsilon)-N\mathfrak c^{k}L(1-k,\varepsilon(\mathfrak c\,\cdot))$ is $\ell$-integral, for $\mathfrak c$ prime to $\ell$ and $k\ge1$. \emph{Conductor a power of $\ell$ and rational values; the published theorem allows any conductor and $\ell$-adic values.} & restricted & \cite{deligne1980values,cassounogues1979valeurs}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Klingen\allowbreak{}Deligne\allowbreak{}Ribet} & The preceding statement together with the theorem of Siegel and Klingen. \emph{A conjunction whose second part is the restricted statement above.} & restricted & \cite{klingen1962werte,siegel1969berechnung,siegel1970fourierschen,deligne1980values,cassounogues1979valeurs}\\

\leanb{Join\allowbreak{}Out} & A conjunction of five statements internal to the archive, on critical values of Hecke $L$-functions of CM fields and on partial zeta values. & internal & ---\\

\leanb{Ht\allowbreak{}Card} & For a continuous $\ell$-adic representation of dimension $a$ of the Galois group of the host field that is de Rham at a place $w$ above $\ell$, and an embedding $\tau$ inducing $w$: the multiset of $\tau$-Hodge--Tate weights has $a$ elements. \emph{Stated for the host fields of the archive's data; the fact holds for every de Rham representation.} & restricted & \cite{fontaine1994semistables,fontaine1982certains}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Ab\allowbreak{}Mul\allowbreak{}NSt} & An abelian variety of dimension $g$ over an algebraically closed field has exactly $n^{2g}$ points killed by $n$, for $n$ invertible in the field. \emph{The classical count of torsion points.} & general & \cite{mumford1970abelian,weil1948varietes}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Abelian\allowbreak{}De\allowbreak{}Rham} & For an abelian scheme $A$ of relative dimension $g$ over a ring $R$: $H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(A/R)$ is finite projective of rank $2g$ and cup product identifies its second exterior power with $H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}$; the submodule of primitive classes is a direct summand, finite projective of rank $g$; both are compatible with base change; the comparison map along a nilpotent divided-power thickening is bijective; and the pairing of a polarisation vanishes on the filtration and is perfect when the polarisation has trivial kernel. \emph{Five standard facts, over an arbitrary affine base.} & general & \cite{oda1969first,berthelot1982theorie,mazur1974universal}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{De\allowbreak{}Rham\allowbreak{}Pot\allowbreak{}Semistable} & Every continuous de Rham representation of the Galois group of a finite extension of $\Q_\ell$ is potentially semistable. \emph{The $p$-adic monodromy theorem for finite extensions of $\Q_\ell$.} & general & \cite{berger2002representations,andre2002filtrations,mebkhout2002analogue,kedlaya2004padic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]

\leanb{Hecke\allowbreak{}LAdic\allowbreak{}Character\allowbreak{}De\allowbreak{}Rham} & The $\ell$-adic character attached to an algebraic Hecke character is de Rham at every place above $\ell$, with Hodge--Tate weights given by the infinity type. \emph{Every algebraic Hecke character of every number field.} & general & \cite{serre1968abelian,fontaine1994semistables}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Algebraic\allowbreak{}Character\allowbreak{}WD} & Local--global compatibility for algebraic Hecke characters at every finite place, including those above $\ell$: the Weil--Deligne representation of the $\ell$-adic character at $w$ is the local component composed with the local Artin map. \emph{Every finite place, those above $\ell$ included.} & general & \cite{serre1968abelian,fontaine1994potentiellement}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]

\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Ar\allowbreak{}Degree} & Two statements on arithmetic intersection numbers and Chern degrees. \emph{Birational invariance of arithmetic self-intersection and the Chern--Weil formula for the degree, two standard facts.} & general & \cite{bost1994heights,gillet1990arithmetic,chern1946characteristic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Principalisation} & For a smooth projective integral variety over a field of characteristic $0$ and a non-zero ideal sheaf $I$: a sequence of blow-ups in smooth centres over the support of $I$ is an isomorphism away from the support and turns $I$ into an effective Cartier divisor with simple normal crossings. \emph{Smooth projective varieties; Hironaka's theorem needs no projectivity.} & restricted & \cite{hironaka1964resolution,hironaka1964resolutionII}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Arith\allowbreak{}Hilbert\allowbreak{}Samuel} & For a nef Hermitian line bundle $\bar L$ of arithmetic self-intersection $a$ on an arithmetic variety of relative dimension $D$, and any $\bar N$: the number of sections of $\bar L^{m}\otimes\bar N$ of sup-norm at most $1$ is finite for large $m$ and its logarithm is $\tfrac{a}{(D+1)!}m^{D+1}+o(m^{D+1})$. \emph{The nef form, which is Moriwaki's.} & general & \cite{gillet1992arithmetic,abbes1995theoreme,zhang1995positive,moriwaki2009continuity}\\

\leanb{Automorphic\allowbreak{}Forms\allowbreak{}Finite\allowbreak{}GL} & Over a totally complex field, the automorphic forms on $\GL_a$ of a given level, $K_\infty$-type and infinitesimal character span a finite-dimensional space. \emph{$\GL_a$ over totally complex fields; Harish-Chandra's theorem covers reductive groups over any number field.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1968automorphic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Base\allowbreak{}Change\allowbreak{}Isobaric\allowbreak{}Transfer} & Base change from a definite unitary group to an isobaric sum on $\GL_n$. \emph{Weak base change from a definite unitary group, under hypotheses of the kind Labesse makes.} & general & \cite{labesse2011changement}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Base\allowbreak{}Change\allowbreak{}Definite\allowbreak{}Unitary\allowbreak{}Group} & The same with the full induced product as local component. \emph{The same with irreducible local components.} & general & \cite{labesse2011changement,bernstein1984pinvariant}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Bernstein\allowbreak{}Unitary\allowbreak{}Product\allowbreak{}Irreducible} & Over a non-archimedean local field, the parabolically induced product of two irreducible unitarisable smooth representations of general linear groups is irreducible. \emph{Bernstein's theorem, which is about general linear groups.} & general & \cite{bernstein1984pinvariant}\\

\leanb{Brauer\allowbreak{}Degree\allowbreak{}Zero} & For a representation $\rho$ of a finite group, $\chi_\rho-\dim\rho$ is an integral combination of differences $\mathrm{Ind}(\chi_i)-\mathrm{Ind}(1)$ with $\chi_i$ characters of degree one of subgroups. \emph{The degree-zero form of Brauer's induction theorem.} & general & \cite{brauer1947artin,deligne1973constantes}\\

\leanb{CMCurve\allowbreak{}Good\allowbreak{}Outside\allowbreak{}Prime\allowbreak{}St} & For a prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$, $p>3$, there is an elliptic curve over $\Q(j(\cO_K))$, $K=\Q(\sqrt{-p})$, with complex multiplication by $\cO_K$, good reduction outside $p$ and minimal discriminant $-p^3$. \emph{Gross's curve $A(p)$.} & general & \cite{gross1982minimal,gross1980arithmetic}\\

\leanb{Ess\allowbreak{}Square\allowbreak{}Integrable\allowbreak{}Segments} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$, an irreducible smooth representation of $\GL_n$ is essentially square-integrable exactly when it is the quotient $L(\Delta)$ attached to a segment. \emph{Characteristic $0$; the theorem holds for every non-archimedean local field.} & restricted & \cite{zelevinsky1980induced,bernstein1977induced}\\

\leanb{Pair\allowbreak{}UAlt} & For a CM field $E$ and a regular algebraic cuspidal representation $\pi$ of $\GL_a$ forming a polarised pair, there is a continuous semisimple $r\colon G_E\to\GL_a(\overline{\Q}_\ell)$ attached to $\pi$ with stated compatibilities. \emph{The Galois representation exists, with compatibility away from $\ell$ only in part: equal dimension, equality when the local parameter is a sum of characters with trivial monodromy, and agreement on inertia for a class of tame parameters.} & restricted & \cite{chenevier2013construction,shin2011galois,caraiani2012local,barnetlamb2012local,barnetlamb2014local,barnetlamb2014potential}\\

\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Clozel\allowbreak{}Purity} & Over a totally complex field, for a cuspidal representation of $\GL_a$ with algebraic infinitesimal characters there is an integer $w_0$ with $\mathrm{infChar}(\bar\tau)=w_0-\mathrm{infChar}(\tau)$ for every embedding $\tau$. \emph{Totally complex fields.} & restricted & \cite{clozel1990motifs}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Complex\allowbreak{}Multiplication\allowbreak{}JSt} & For $K$ imaginary quadratic there are a Hilbert class field $H\subset\C$ and an Artin isomorphism $\mathrm{Cl}(K)\cong\Gal(H/K)$ with $K(j(\mathfrak a))=H$ and $\mathrm{art}([\mathfrak b])\,j(\mathfrak a)=j(\mathfrak b^{-1}\mathfrak a)$. \emph{The main theorem of complex multiplication for $j$-invariants of ideal lattices.} & general & \cite{hasse1927neue,shimura1971introduction}\\

\leanb{Depth\allowbreak{}Zero\allowbreak{}Jacquet\allowbreak{}Injective} & Over a non-archimedean local field, for an irreducible representation of $\GL_n$ and a standard parabolic subgroup: a vector fixed by the first congruence subgroup and by the integral points of the unipotent radical, whose image in the Jacquet module is zero, is zero. \emph{$\GL_n$ at depth zero, and only injectivity.} & restricted & \cite{moy1996jacquet}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Depth\allowbreak{}Zero\allowbreak{}Support} & Over a non-archimedean local field, if an irreducible representation of $\GL_n$ has a non-zero vector fixed by the first congruence subgroup, so has every member of its cuspidal support. \emph{$\GL_n$ at depth zero.} & restricted & \cite{moy1994unrefined,moy1996jacquet}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Classification} & For the real unitary groups $\U(p,q)$: every Harish-Chandra parameter carries an irreducible unitary square-integrable representation with that infinitesimal character and a unique lowest $K$-type, with stated uniqueness. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$, with a weaker statement on $K$-types than Schmid's.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1965discrete,harishchandra1966discrete,schmid1975some}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Cover} & For the double cover of $\U(p,q)$ defined by a square root of the determinant: the discrete series is a family $D(\lambda)$ indexed by parameters, with prescribed $K$-types, and every discrete series representation is equivalent to one of them. \emph{A double cover of $\U(p,q)$.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1965discrete,harishchandra1966discrete,schmid1975some}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Cover\allowbreak{}Exists} & For that double cover and every parameter $\lambda$ there is a discrete series representation with parameter $\lambda$. \emph{A double cover of $\U(p,q)$.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1966discrete,schmid1975some}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Exists} & The same as \lean{DiscreteSeriesUpqExists} below. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1966discrete,schmid1975some}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Hermitian\allowbreak{}Unique} & Two discrete series representations of $\U(p,q)$ with the same Harish-Chandra parameter, transported to the unitary group of a Hermitian matrix by two frames, are unitarily equivalent. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$ and their conjugates.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1966discrete}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Lowest\allowbreak{}KType} & In a discrete series representation of $\U(p,q)$ with Harish-Chandra parameter $\lambda$, the $K$-type of highest weight $\lambda+\rho_n-\rho_c$ occurs with multiplicity one, with a second clause on its uniqueness. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$.} & restricted & \cite{schmid1975some,harishchandra1966discrete}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Upq\allowbreak{}Exists} & For every Harish-Chandra parameter $\lambda$ of $\U(p,q)$ there is an irreducible unitary representation with square-integrable matrix coefficients that contains the $K$-type $\lambda+\rho_n-\rho_c$, with a clause on its other $K$-types. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1966discrete,schmid1975some}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Dixmier\allowbreak{}Malliavin\allowbreak{}Factorisation} & For a group closed in $\GL_n(\C)$ with a Haar measure, every smooth compactly supported function is a finite sum of convolutions of two such functions, the first supported in a prescribed neighbourhood of the identity. \emph{Closed linear groups; the theorem is for all Lie groups.} & restricted & \cite{dixmier1978factorisations}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Eisenstein\allowbreak{}Continuation} & For a Hermitian space $V$ of positive rank over a CM extension, the Siegel Eisenstein series on the doubled group $\U(V\oplus-V)$ attached to a section of the degenerate principal series continues meromorphically, with poles of finite order. \emph{Siegel Eisenstein series on doubled unitary groups; Langlands's theorem is for all Eisenstein series.} & restricted & \cite{langlands1976functional,moeglin1994decomposition}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Doubling\allowbreak{}Method\allowbreak{}Local\allowbreak{}Zeta\allowbreak{}Integrals} & The preceding statement together with the basic identity of the doubling method. \emph{The global identity of the doubling method with the continuation above; nothing about local zeta integrals, despite the name.} & differs & \cite{gelbart1987explicit,langlands1976functional}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Flath\allowbreak{}Tensor\allowbreak{}Product} & Every irreducible unitary representation of the adelic unitary group of a Hermitian space over a CM extension is a restricted tensor product of irreducible unitary representations of the local groups. \emph{Unitary groups of Hermitian spaces over CM extensions.} & restricted & \cite{flath1979decomposition}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Unitary\allowbreak{}Irreducible\allowbreak{}Admissible} & Every irreducible unitary representation of a non-archimedean local unitary group of that kind is admissible. \emph{These unitary groups; Bernstein's theorem is for reductive groups.} & restricted & \cite{bernstein1974all}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Flath\allowbreak{}Factorisation} & The factorisation of \lean{FlathTensorProduct}, with the local factors unramified at almost all places. \emph{These unitary groups.} & restricted & \cite{flath1979decomposition}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Fontaine\allowbreak{}Bcris} & Seven properties of Fontaine's ring $B_{\mathrm{cris}}$, among them injectivity of Frobenius and of $B_{\mathrm{cris}}\to B_{\mathrm{dR}}$ and the fundamental exact sequence. \emph{Seven standard properties of $B_{\mathrm{cris}}$.} & general & \cite{fontaine1982certains,fontaine1994corps,fontaine1994semistables}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Formal\allowbreak{}Algebraisation} & Grothendieck's algebraisation over a complete noetherian ring, for morphisms from a proper scheme and for schemes. \emph{Grothendieck's existence theorem.} & general & \cite{grothendieck1961elements}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Formal\allowbreak{}Degree\allowbreak{}Compact\allowbreak{}Dual} & With the Haar measure of $\U(p,q)$ normalised through the compact dual, the formal degree of the discrete series representation with Harish-Chandra parameter $\lambda$ is given by the product formula in the differences $\lambda_a-\lambda_b$. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1966discrete,atiyah1977geometric}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{GKGlobalisation} & For unitary representations of $\U(p,q)$: the closure of an admissible $(\mathfrak g,K)$-submodule is stable under the group, and infinitesimally equivalent irreducible unitary representations are unitarily equivalent. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1953representations}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{GLHowe\allowbreak{}Duality} & For $n,n'\ge1$, the polynomial functions on $n\times n'$ matrices decompose under $\GL_n(\C)\times\GL_{n'}(\C)$, and under $\U(n)\times\U(n')$, as the multiplicity-free sum of the $F_n^{a}\otimes F_{n'}^{a}$. \emph{The duality of $\GL_n$ and $\GL_{n'}$ on polynomials.} & general & \cite{howe1989remarks}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cusp\allowbreak{}UAlt} & For a CM field $E$ and a regular algebraic cuspidal representation $\pi$ of $\GL_a$ polarised by a Hecke character, there is a continuous semisimple $r\colon G_E\to\GL_a(\overline{\Q}_\ell)$ attached to $\pi$ with stated compatibilities. \emph{The Galois representation exists, with compatibility away from $\ell$ only in part: equal dimension, equality when the local parameter is a sum of characters with trivial monodromy, and agreement on inertia for a class of tame parameters; the literature gives full compatibility.} & restricted & \cite{clozel2011construction,shin2011galois,chenevier2013construction,taylor2007compatibility,caraiani2012local,barnetlamb2012local,barnetlamb2014local,caraiani2014monodromy,barnetlamb2014potential}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Generic\allowbreak{}Unitary\allowbreak{}Dual\allowbreak{}GL} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$, every irreducible unitarisable generic representation of $\GL_N$ is a product of unitary segment representations and of complementary pairs. \emph{Characteristic $0$.} & restricted & \cite{tadic1986classification,bernstein1984pinvariant}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Geometric\allowbreak{}Lemma\allowbreak{}Filtration} & The filtration half of the geometric lemma for $\GL_n$ over a non-archimedean local field. \emph{The filtration half of the geometric lemma.} & restricted & \cite{bernstein1977induced,zelevinsky1980induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Good\allowbreak{}Chern\allowbreak{}Weil} & For a metric that is good in Mumford's sense, Chern--Weil integrals compute Chern numbers, with a push-forward formula on flag bundles. \emph{Mumford's theorem for good metrics and the push-forward formula for flag bundles, in the archive's coordinates.} & general & \cite{mumford1977hirzebruch,brion1996pushforward}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Green\allowbreak{}Cuspidal} & The cuspidal characters of $\GL_d(\F_p)$ are parametrised without repetition by the monic irreducible polynomials of degree $d$ with non-zero constant term, each of degree $\prod_{i=1}^{d-1}(p^i-1)$. \emph{Prime fields; Green's theorem is for every finite field.} & restricted & \cite{green1955characters}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Green\allowbreak{}Regular\allowbreak{}Characters} & For $K=\F_{p^d}$, each regular character $\theta$ of $K^\times$ gives a cuspidal character of $\GL_d(\F_p)$ of degree $\prod_{i=1}^{d-1}(p^i-1)$ with value $(-1)^{d-1}\sum_i\theta(z^{p^i})$ on elements with irreducible characteristic polynomial; $\tau(\theta)=\tau(\theta')$ exactly for Frobenius conjugates; and every cuspidal character arises. \emph{Prime fields.} & restricted & \cite{green1955characters}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Green\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}St} & For a prime $p$ and $N\ge1$ there is a map from square-free polynomials of degree $N$ to irreducible characters of $\GL_N(\F_p)$ with stated properties. \emph{Prime fields.} & restricted & \cite{green1955characters}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Abelian\allowbreak{}Lifting} & For a surjection of rings whose kernel has nilpotent divided powers, abelian schemes and their homomorphisms lift according to the Hodge filtration in crystalline cohomology. \emph{The lifting half of the theory of Grothendieck and Messing.} & general & \cite{grothendieck1971groupes,messing1972crystals,mazur1974universal}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Grothendieck\allowbreak{}Deformation} & For every surjection of rings with nilpotent divided-power kernel: the Grothendieck--Messing statement on canonicity of the comparison and on lifting abelian schemes and their homomorphisms. \emph{The theory of Grothendieck and Messing for abelian schemes.} & general & \cite{grothendieck1971groupes,messing1972crystals,mazur1974universal}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Grothendieck\allowbreak{}Messing} & The same for rings in which a prime $p$ is nilpotent. \emph{The same when a prime is nilpotent.} & general & \cite{grothendieck1971groupes,messing1972crystals,mazur1974universal}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{principal\allowbreak{}Polarisation\allowbreak{}One\allowbreak{}Section} & For a principally polarised abelian variety over an algebraically closed field, the space of sections of the polarising line bundle is one-dimensional. \emph{A classical consequence of Riemann--Roch on abelian varieties.} & general & \cite{mumford1970abelian}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Harish\allowbreak{}Chandra\allowbreak{}Analyticity} & Matrix coefficients of $K$-finite vectors in admissible representations of $\U(p,q)$ are real-analytic, with a density statement for Levi subgroups. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$ and their Levi subgroups.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1953representations}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Harish\allowbreak{}Chandra\allowbreak{}Finite} & On the adelic unitary group of a Hermitian space over a CM extension, the automorphic forms of a given level, archimedean $K$-type and infinitesimal character span a finite-dimensional space. \emph{Unitary groups of Hermitian spaces over CM extensions.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1968automorphic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Harish\allowbreak{}Chandra\allowbreak{}Modules} & For the double covers of $\U(p,q)$: the Harish-Chandra module of an irreducible unitary representation exists, is admissible and irreducible, and determines the representation; $K$-finite vectors are analytic. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$ and their double covers.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1953representations,harishchandra1954representations2,harishchandra1954representations3}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hasse\allowbreak{}Norm\allowbreak{}St} & For a number field $F$ and $\delta,x\ne0$: if $x=a^2-\delta b^2$ is solvable at every real place and in every non-archimedean completion, it is solvable in $F$. \emph{Quadratic extensions; the norm theorem is for cyclic extensions.} & restricted & \cite{hasse1924darstellbarkeit,hasse1931beweis}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hecke\allowbreak{}LAdic\allowbreak{}Character} & For every number field there is a global Artin map, and for every algebraic Hecke character and every $\ell$ a unique continuous $\ell$-adic character attached to it through that map. \emph{Every number field and every algebraic Hecke character.} & general & \cite{weil1956certain,taniyama1957lfunctions,serre1968abelian,takagi1920theorie,artin1927beweis,chevalley1940theorie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hecke\allowbreak{}LAdic\allowbreak{}Character\allowbreak{}Crystalline} & The $\ell$-adic character of an algebraic Hecke character is crystalline at every place above $\ell$ at which the Hecke character is unramified. \emph{Every place above $\ell$ at which the character is unramified.} & general & \cite{serre1968abelian,fontaine1982certains}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hecke\allowbreak{}LAdic\allowbreak{}Character\allowbreak{}Above} & At the places above $\ell$, the $\ell$-adic character of an algebraic Hecke character is de Rham, potentially crystalline, and crystalline where the Hecke character is unramified, with the expected Hodge--Tate weights. \emph{The properties at the places above $\ell$.} & general & \cite{serre1968abelian,fontaine1982certains,fontaine1994semistables}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hecke\allowbreak{}LAdic\allowbreak{}Parameter\allowbreak{}Above\allowbreak{}Alt} & At a place $w$ above $\ell$, the Weil--Deligne representation given by Fontaine's $D_{\mathrm{pst}}$ for the $\ell$-adic character of an algebraic Hecke character is its local component composed with local class field theory. \emph{Compatibility at the places above $\ell$ for $\GL_1$.} & general & \cite{serre1968abelian,fontaine1994potentiellement}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hecke\allowbreak{}LEntire\allowbreak{}And\allowbreak{}Nonzero\allowbreak{}At\allowbreak{}One} & For a unitary Hecke character $\chi$ of a number field: if $\chi$ is not a power of the norm, $L(s,\chi)$ is entire; and if $\chi\ne1$, $L(1,\chi)\ne0$. \emph{Every unitary Hecke character of every number field.} & general & \cite{hecke1918neue,hecke1920neue,tate1967fourier}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hecke\allowbreak{}LPartial\allowbreak{}Continuation} & For a number field and a finite set $T$ of places: the $L$-function with the Euler factors at $T$ removed of a unitary Hecke character that is not a power of the norm is entire and non-zero on $\re s\ge1$; and $(s-1)\zeta_K^{T}(s)$ is entire and non-zero there. \emph{The same with finitely many Euler factors removed.} & general & \cite{hecke1918neue,hecke1920neue,landau1903neuer}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hermitian\allowbreak{}Hasse\allowbreak{}Principle} & For a quadratic extension of number fields, two non-degenerate Hermitian matrices that are congruent over every completion are congruent. \emph{Landherr's theorem.} & general & \cite{landherr1936aquivalenz}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hermitian\allowbreak{}Local\allowbreak{}Global} & Locally, over a quadratic extension of non-archimedean local fields with $2\ne0$, two non-degenerate Hermitian forms of the same rank are congruent exactly when the ratio of their determinants is a norm; with a global statement over CM fields. \emph{The local classification and Landherr's global theorem.} & general & \cite{jacobowitz1962hermitian,landherr1936aquivalenz}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Holomorphic\allowbreak{}Discrete\allowbreak{}Series} & A discrete series representation of $\U(p,q)$ with Harish-Chandra parameter in the holomorphic chamber is a lowest-weight module. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1955representations4,harishchandra1956representations5,harishchandra1956representations6}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Howe\allowbreak{}Duality\allowbreak{}Real} & For a unitary dual pair over a CM extension, Howe duality at the archimedean places in the polynomial Fock model of the Weil representation. \emph{Unitary dual pairs, and only the lift of the trivial representation.} & restricted & \cite{howe1989transcending}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Ideal\allowbreak{}Invariants\allowbreak{}One\allowbreak{}Orbit\allowbreak{}St} & For $K$ imaginary quadratic and a lattice homothetic to a fractional ideal, $j$ is algebraic over $K$ and its orbit under $\mathrm{Aut}(\C/K)$ is the set of $j$-invariants of all ideal lattices. \emph{The classical statement on the conjugates of $j$.} & general & \cite{hasse1927neue,shimura1971introduction}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Induced\allowbreak{}Simple\allowbreak{}Lowest\allowbreak{}Alcove} & For $\GL_N$ in characteristic $p$ and a dominant weight $\lambda$ with $\lambda_i-\lambda_j+(j-i)\le p$ for $i<j$, the induced module $\nabla(\lambda)$ is non-zero and simple. \emph{$\GL_N$; the statement holds for reductive groups.} & restricted & \cite{andersen1980strong,jantzen2003representations}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Jacquet\allowbreak{}Shalika} & The rigidity statement \lean{JacquetShalikaRigidity} together with a bound on Satake parameters of cuspidal representations. \emph{Totally complex fields.} & restricted & \cite{jacquet1981eulerI,jacquet1981eulerII}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{KFinite\allowbreak{}Vectors\allowbreak{}Unitary} & Every irreducible unitary representation of $\U(p,q)$ is admissible; its $K$-finite vectors are analytic, dense, stable under the Lie algebra and irreducible as a $(\mathfrak g,K)$-module. \emph{The groups $\U(p,q)$.} & restricted & \cite{harishchandra1953representations,harishchandra1954representations2,harishchandra1954representations3}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Kawamata\allowbreak{}Viehweg} & For a smooth projective variety $X$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$ and a nef and big line bundle $N$: $H^q(X,K_X\otimes N)=0$ for $q>0$. \emph{The vanishing theorem for nef and big line bundles.} & general & \cite{kawamata1982generalization,viehweg1982vanishing}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Kudla\allowbreak{}Splitting\allowbreak{}Split\allowbreak{}Unitary} & For a quadratic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic $0$, a Hermitian matrix $Q$ and a character $\chi$ of $E^\times$ restricting to the right power of the quadratic character: a smooth unitary representation of the split unitary group $\mathrm{U}(\nu,\nu)$ itself on the Schwartz space of the Schrödinger model, compatible with the Heisenberg action attached to $Q$ and given on the Levi subgroup by the usual formula. \emph{The split member $\mathrm{U}(\nu,\nu)$ of the pair only; Kudla's splitting covers both members of a unitary dual pair; stated in characteristic $0$.} & restricted & \cite{kudla1994splitting,harris1996theta}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{L2\allowbreak{}Extension\allowbreak{}Log\allowbreak{}Canonical} & An extension theorem of Ohsawa--Takegoshi type with $L^2$ estimates, from a finite non-degenerate common zero set of $n$ sections of a line bundle on a compact complex manifold of dimension $n$. \emph{Extension from a finite set of points; the theorems of Ohsawa--Takegoshi type cover subvarieties.} & restricted & \cite{ohsawa1987extension,demailly2016extension,cao2017general}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Landherr\allowbreak{}St} & For a CM field, two non-degenerate Hermitian matrices with the same signature at every embedding and with determinants differing by a norm are congruent. \emph{Landherr's classification over a CM field.} & general & \cite{landherr1936aquivalenz}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Linnik} & There are $C,L>0$ such that for coprime $a,q\ge1$ the least prime $p\equiv a\pmod q$ is at most $C\,q^{L}$. \emph{Linnik's theorem.} & general & \cite{linnik1944least1,linnik1944least2}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cuspidal\allowbreak{}Multiplicity\allowbreak{}One} & Over a totally complex field, two cuspidal automorphic subrepresentations of $\GL_a$ in the same isomorphism class have the same space. \emph{Totally complex fields.} & restricted & \cite{shalika1974multiplicity,piatetskishapiro1979multiplicity}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Car\allowbreak{}UAlt} & For a CM field $E$ and a conjugate self-dual regular algebraic cuspidal representation of $\GL_a$, $a\ge2$: the attached $r\colon G_E\to\GL_a(\overline{\Q}_\ell)$ exists with the compatibilities of \lean{CuspUAlt} and with stated properties at the places above $\ell$. \emph{As \lean{CuspUAlt}: compatibility away from $\ell$ only in part.} & restricted & \cite{clozel2011construction,shin2011galois,chenevier2013construction,taylor2007compatibility,caraiani2012local,barnetlamb2012local,barnetlamb2014local,caraiani2014monodromy,barnetlamb2014potential}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Car\allowbreak{}UAlt} & The same statement as \leanb{Car\allowbreak{}UAlt} above, entered a second time in the file. & repeated & \cite{clozel2011construction,shin2011galois,chenevier2013construction,taylor2007compatibility,caraiani2012local,barnetlamb2012local,barnetlamb2014local,caraiani2014monodromy,barnetlamb2014potential}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Metaplectic\allowbreak{}Representation} & For every $n$ there is a two-sheeted covering group of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\R)$ with a unitary representation on $L^2(\R^n)$, continuous on Schwartz space and compatible with the Schr\"odinger representation of the Heisenberg group. \emph{The oscillator representation of the metaplectic group.} & general & \cite{weil1964certains,shale1962linear,segal1963transforms}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Moy\allowbreak{}Prasad\allowbreak{}Jacquet\allowbreak{}Iso} & Over a non-archimedean local field, for an admissible representation of $\GL_n$ and a standard parabolic subgroup: the vectors fixed by the first congruence subgroup and the integral points of the unipotent radical map bijectively onto the corresponding fixed vectors of the Jacquet module. \emph{$\GL_n$ at depth zero.} & restricted & \cite{moy1996jacquet}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Nadel\allowbreak{}Vanishing\allowbreak{}And\allowbreak{}Non\allowbreak{}Klt\allowbreak{}Divisor} & Nadel vanishing for a pair, and the existence of a divisor with an isolated non-klt point, on a normal projective complex variety. \emph{Vanishing for some ideal with the right support, which is weaker than Nadel's theorem for the multiplier ideal.} & restricted & \cite{nadel1990multiplier,angehrn1995effective,kollar1997singularities}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Nef\allowbreak{}Numerics} & Over an algebraically closed field: intersection numbers of nef line bundles are non-negative; a nef line bundle is big exactly when its top self-intersection is positive; and an asymptotic Riemann--Roch statement for nef bundles. \emph{Three standard facts on nef line bundles.} & general & \cite{kleiman1966toward,lazarsfeld2004positivity}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Point\allowbreak{}Separation\allowbreak{}Pair} & An effective criterion of Angehrn--Siu type for a line bundle on a klt pair to separate two points of a normal projective complex variety. \emph{The criterion of Angehrn and Siu in Koll\'ar's numerical form, with his constants.} & general & \cite{angehrn1995effective,kollar1997singularities}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Poitou\allowbreak{}Tate\allowbreak{}Normalised} & Poitou--Tate duality with normalised local invariant maps, for finite modules over a number field and a set of primes containing those above $\ell$. \emph{$\ell$-power torsion modules, with $\ell\ne2$ or the field totally complex.} & restricted & \cite{tate1963duality,poitou1966remarques,milne1986arithmetic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Prismatic\allowbreak{}Dieudonne\allowbreak{}Hodge} & For a complete algebraically closed field of mixed characteristic, a prismatic Dieudonn\'e functor from $p$-divisible groups over its ring of integers to finite free $A_{\inf}$-modules, with its Hodge-theoretic properties. \emph{Over the ring of integers of a complete algebraically closed field; the theory is over quasi-syntomic rings.} & restricted & \cite{anschutz2023prismatic,bhatt2018integral,scholze2013moduli}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Quadratic\allowbreak{}Class\allowbreak{}Field\allowbreak{}Theory} & Class field theory for quadratic extensions of number fields: local norm-residue characters, the Hasse norm theorem, an exact sequence and the product formula, with a compatibility in towers. \emph{Class field theory for quadratic extensions, which is what the name says.} & general & \cite{hilbert1899theorie,hasse1924darstellbarkeit,takagi1920theorie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Radford\allowbreak{}Shuffle\allowbreak{}Polynomial} & In characteristic $0$, the shuffle algebra on an ordered alphabet is the polynomial algebra on the Lyndon words. \emph{Radford's theorem.} & general & \cite{radford1979natural}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Weil\allowbreak{}Unitary\allowbreak{}Convergent} & The Siegel--Weil formula for unitary groups in the convergent range, for Hermitian spaces of ranks $n<m\le2n$ satisfying Weil's condition: the theta integral converges and equals the value of a Siegel Eisenstein series. \emph{Ichino's range $n<m\le2n$ under Weil's condition.} & general & \cite{ichino2007siegel,weil1965formule,ikeda1996residue}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Weil\allowbreak{}Theta\allowbreak{}Convergence} & Weil's criterion: if $V$ is anisotropic or $n+r(V)<\dim V$, the theta integral over $[\U(V)]$ of every adelic Schwartz function on $V^n$ converges absolutely. \emph{Weil's criterion.} & general & \cite{weil1965formule}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Rallis\allowbreak{}Inner\allowbreak{}Product\allowbreak{}Convergent} & The Rallis inner product formula in the convergent range, for theta lifts between unitary groups of ranks $n<m\le2n$ under Weil's condition. \emph{The convergent range, for unitary pairs.} & general & \cite{rallis1984injectivity,li1992nonvanishing}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Ray\allowbreak{}Character\allowbreak{}Artin} & A homomorphism from the ideals prime to $\mathfrak m$ to an abelian group that is trivial on principal ideals generated by elements congruent to $1$ modulo $\mathfrak m$ is given by a unique continuous character of the Galois group, unramified outside $\mathfrak m$, through Frobenius elements. \emph{Artin reciprocity for ray class characters.} & general & \cite{takagi1920theorie,artin1927beweis}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Ray\allowbreak{}Class\allowbreak{}Field\allowbreak{}St} & Existence of the ray class field of a number field for a non-zero ideal, with its Artin map. \emph{Existence of ray class fields.} & general & \cite{takagi1920theorie,artin1927beweis}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Real\allowbreak{}Metaplectic\allowbreak{}Representation} & A topological double cover of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\R)$ with a strongly continuous unitary representation on $L^2(\R^n)$ in which the non-trivial element of the kernel acts by $-1$, compatible with the Schr\"odinger representation and preserving Schwartz space. \emph{The oscillator representation.} & general & \cite{segal1959foundations,shale1962linear,weil1964certains}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Regular\allowbreak{}Algebraic\allowbreak{}Purity} & For a CM field, a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\GL_a$ has pure infinity type and is cohomological. \emph{CM fields; Clozel's lemmas are for any number field.} & restricted & \cite{clozel1990motifs}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Schur\allowbreak{}Orthogonality\allowbreak{}Square\allowbreak{}Integrable} & For a unimodular locally compact group and an irreducible unitary representation with one non-zero square-integrable matrix coefficient: all matrix coefficients are square-integrable and satisfy the Schur orthogonality relations with a formal degree. \emph{Godement's theorem for unimodular groups.} & general & \cite{godement1947orthogonalite,godement1947demonstration}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Semi\allowbreak{}Abelian\allowbreak{}Hom\allowbreak{}Extension} & Over a noetherian normal scheme, a homomorphism of semi-abelian schemes defined over a dense open extends uniquely. \emph{Extension of homomorphisms over a normal base.} & general & \cite{faltings1990degeneration}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Semi\allowbreak{}Abelian\allowbreak{}Lie\allowbreak{}Seminegative} & For a semi-abelian scheme $G$ over a smooth projective curve in characteristic $0$, every subbundle of $\mathrm{Lie}\,G$ has non-positive degree. \emph{Bost's semi-negativity in characteristic $0$.} & general & \cite{bost2004germs,bost2006evaluation,griffiths1970periods}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Semistable\allowbreak{}Reduction\allowbreak{}St} & Every polarised abelian variety over a finite extension of $\Q_p$ acquires a semi-abelian model over the integers of a finite extension. \emph{$p$-adic fields and polarised abelian varieties; Grothendieck's theorem is for any discretely valued field.} & restricted & \cite{grothendieck1972groupes}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Serre\allowbreak{}Holomorphic\allowbreak{}Sections} & On a smooth projective complex variety, algebraic sections of a line bundle are the same as holomorphic sections. \emph{Global sections of line bundles on smooth projective varieties; Serre's theorem covers coherent sheaves and all cohomology.} & restricted & \cite{serre1956geometrie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Unused\allowbreak{}Slot72} & The proposition \lean{True}; an empty slot of the file. & empty & ---\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Set\allowbreak{}Unitary} & For a non-degenerate Hermitian form over a CM extension: an Iwasawa decomposition of the adelic unitary group and a Siegel set with the properties of reduction theory. \emph{Unitary groups of Hermitian forms over CM extensions.} & restricted & \cite{borel1962arithmetic,borel1969introduction,moeglin1995spectral}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Toroidal\allowbreak{}Integral} & For $g\ge1$ and odd $n\ge3$: the Siegel moduli scheme of level $n$ over $\Z[1/n,\zeta_n]$ has a smooth projective toroidal compactification carrying a semi-abelian scheme that extends the universal abelian scheme. \emph{Odd levels $n\ge3$.} & restricted & \cite{faltings1990degeneration}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Weil\allowbreak{}Unitary\allowbreak{}Schrodinger} & The Siegel--Weil formula in the Schr\"odinger model of $\U(n,n)$, for $n<\dim V\le2n$ under Weil's condition. \emph{The same formula in another model.} & general & \cite{ichino2007siegel,weil1965formule,ikeda1996residue}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Square\allowbreak{}Integrable\allowbreak{}Segment} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$, every irreducible square-integrable representation of $\GL_n$ is the representation $L(\Delta)$ of a segment. \emph{Characteristic $0$.} & restricted & \cite{zelevinsky1980induced,bernstein1977induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Stone\allowbreak{}Von\allowbreak{}Neumann} & For a symplectic space over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic not $2$: the Heisenberg group has an irreducible smooth representation with a given non-trivial central character, unique up to isomorphism. \emph{The theorem for the Heisenberg group of a non-archimedean local field.} & general & \cite{stone1930linear,vonneumann1931eindeutigkeit,mackey1949theorem,moeglin1987correspondances}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Strong\allowbreak{}Approx\allowbreak{}SU} & Strong approximation for the special unitary group of a non-degenerate Hermitian form of rank at least $2$ over a CM extension, with respect to a set of places at which the group is not compact. \emph{Special unitary groups; the theorem is for simply connected groups.} & restricted & \cite{kneser1965starke,platonov1969problem}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Theta\allowbreak{}Rational\allowbreak{}Invariance} & A statement in the archive's own terms: invariance of spaces of theta functions on CM tori under rational unitary matrices, up to an explicit character. & internal & ---\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Toroidal\allowbreak{}Compactification} & For a unitary moduli problem of PEL type over a CM field: a projective model containing the moduli space as a dense open, smooth of the expected dimension, with boundary a divisor with simple normal crossings and a logarithmic Kodaira--Spencer isomorphism. \emph{Unitary moduli problems of PEL type in characteristic $0$.} & restricted & \cite{ash1975smooth,pink1989arithmetical,lan2013arithmetic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Toroidal\allowbreak{}For\allowbreak{}Fan\allowbreak{}KS} & The same for a prescribed polarised admissible fan without self-intersection, with toroidal charts along the boundary. \emph{The same.} & restricted & \cite{lan2013arithmetic,faltings1990degeneration,ash1975smooth}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Totally\allowbreak{}Disjoint\allowbreak{}Product\allowbreak{}Irreducible} & Over a non-archimedean local field: if no member of the cuspidal support of $\pi_1$ is $\nu^{j}$ times a member of that of $\pi_2$ for $j\in\{-1,0,1\}$, then $\pi_1\times\pi_2$ is irreducible. \emph{An irreducibility criterion in the theory of Bernstein and Zelevinsky.} & general & \cite{bernstein1977induced,zelevinsky1980induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Unlinked\allowbreak{}Product\allowbreak{}Irreducible} & Over a non-archimedean local field: if no member of the cuspidal support of $\pi_1$ is an unramified twist of a member of that of $\pi_2$, then $\pi_1\times\pi_2$ is irreducible. \emph{A hypothesis much stronger than Zelevinsky's unlinked segments.} & restricted & \cite{zelevinsky1980induced,bernstein1977induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Unramified\allowbreak{}Doubling\allowbreak{}GL} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$, for an unramified representation of $\GL_n$ the doubling zeta integral of the normalised spherical section against the zonal spherical function converges for $\re s$ large and is given by the expected quotient of local $L$-factors. \emph{The unramified computation of the doubling integral for $\GL_n$; stated in characteristic $0$.} & general & \cite{piatetskishapiro1987lfunctions}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Vol\allowbreak{}Ge} & For a Hermitian line bundle on an arithmetic variety that is nef on fibres with semipositive metric, the arithmetic volume is at least the arithmetic self-intersection number. \emph{The lower bound for the arithmetic volume of a nef Hermitian line bundle.} & general & \cite{gillet1992arithmetic,zhang1995positive,moriwaki2009continuity}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Vol\allowbreak{}Nef} & For an arithmetically nef Hermitian line bundle, the arithmetic volume equals the arithmetic self-intersection number. \emph{Moriwaki's equality.} & general & \cite{moriwaki2009continuity,zhang1995positive}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Weber\allowbreak{}Ray\allowbreak{}Field\allowbreak{}St} & For $K$ imaginary quadratic of discriminant less than $-4$, the field generated over $K$ by the values of the Weber function at the $n$-torsion points of $\C/\cO_K$ is the ray class field of conductor $n$. \emph{Ray class fields of imaginary quadratic fields by values of the Weber function.} & general & \cite{hasse1927neue,shimura1971introduction}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Weil\allowbreak{}Representation\allowbreak{}Exists} & For a Hermitian and a skew-Hermitian space over a CM extension and Hecke characters with the right restrictions, a Weil representation of the product of the two adelic unitary groups exists. \emph{Existence of the Weil representation of a unitary dual pair.} & general & \cite{weil1964certains,kudla1994splitting}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Weil\allowbreak{}Representation\allowbreak{}Unitary\allowbreak{}Pair} & The same in the notation of the archive's base data. \emph{The same.} & general & \cite{weil1964certains,kudla1994splitting}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Weil\allowbreak{}Siegel\allowbreak{}Formula\allowbreak{}Unitary} & Weil's formula for unitary groups: under Weil's condition the theta integral is bounded by a continuous seminorm and converges, and in the range $2n<m$ it equals the Siegel Eisenstein series. \emph{Weil's formula in his range.} & general & \cite{weil1965formule}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Weyl\allowbreak{}Branching} & The restriction to $\GL_n(\C)$, and to $\U(n)$, of the irreducible representation of $\GL_{n+1}(\C)$ of highest weight $\lambda$ is the multiplicity-free sum over the weights interlacing $\lambda$. \emph{Weyl's branching rule.} & general & \cite{weyl1946classical}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Dual\allowbreak{}Abelian\allowbreak{}Scheme} & Every abelian scheme has a dual abelian scheme of the same relative dimension, with a Poincar\'e bundle exhibiting each as the dual of the other. \emph{Existence of the dual abelian scheme.} & general & \cite{mumford1965geometric,faltings1990degeneration}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Zarhin\allowbreak{}Statement} & Over the valuation ring of an algebraically closed non-archimedean field, an abelian scheme with a relatively ample line bundle is a retract of a principally polarised one. \emph{Over the valuation ring of an algebraically closed non-archimedean field.} & restricted & \cite{zarhin1977endomorphisms,moretbailly1985pinceaux}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Fargues\allowbreak{}Exact} & For a $p$-divisible group over the ring of integers of a complete algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$: the kernel of the Hodge--Tate map is the annihilator, under the pairing induced by the Weil pairing, of the corresponding part of the dual. \emph{The statement of Fargues on the kernel of the Hodge--Tate map.} & general & \cite{fargues2008isomorphisme,tate1967pdivisible}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Nef\allowbreak{}RR} & An asymptotic Riemann--Roch statement for a divisor class that is nef on the generic fibre of an arithmetic variety: $D!\,\dim H^0(\tau a)/\tau^{D}$ tends to the generic degree. \emph{The asymptotic Riemann--Roch statement of \lean{NefNumerics}, on the generic fibre of an arithmetic variety.} & restricted & \cite{lazarsfeld2004positivity,kleiman1966toward}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Poincare\allowbreak{}Lelong\allowbreak{}Inv} & A Poincar\'e--Lelong formula on an arithmetic variety: the integral of $\log\norm{s}$ against Chern forms equals a sum over the horizontal components of the divisor of $s$, with a correction. \emph{A form of the Poincar\'e--Lelong formula used for heights; its exact shape was not compared with a published formula.} & restricted & \cite{lelong1957integration,bost1994heights}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Principalisation\allowbreak{}Char\allowbreak{}Zero} & For a smooth separated quasi-compact scheme over a field of characteristic $0$, an ideal sheaf and a divisor with simple normal crossings: a sequence of blow-ups in smooth centres having normal crossings with the divisor makes the ideal an effective Cartier divisor with simple normal crossings. \emph{Principalisation compatible with a divisor with simple normal crossings.} & general & \cite{hironaka1964resolution,hironaka1964resolutionII,kollar2007lectures}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Resolution\allowbreak{}Char\allowbreak{}Zero} & Every reduced separated scheme of finite type over a field of characteristic $0$ has a resolution by a sequence of blow-ups that is an isomorphism over the smooth locus, the preimage of the singular locus being a divisor with simple normal crossings. \emph{Hironaka's theorem.} & general & \cite{hironaka1964resolution,hironaka1964resolutionII,kollar2007lectures}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cheb} & For a number field $F$, an open normal subgroup $U$ of $G_F$, $g\in G_F$ and a finite set of primes: there is a prime outside the set, of degree one and unramified over $\Q$, with inertia in $U$ and a Frobenius in $gU$. \emph{An existence statement that follows from the density theorem.} & restricted & \cite{chebotarev1926bestimmung}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Eis\allowbreak{}BL} & Siegel Eisenstein series on the doubled unitary group attached to standard sections converge in a half-plane and continue meromorphically, with poles of finite order. \emph{Siegel Eisenstein series on doubled unitary groups.} & restricted & \cite{bernstein2024meromorphic,langlands1976functional}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Weil\allowbreak{}Std} & The Siegel--Weil formula for a definite Hermitian or skew-Hermitian space: the Siegel Eisenstein series is holomorphic at $s_0=(m-n)/2$ and its value there is a constant times the theta integral. \emph{The Siegel--Weil formula for a definite space.} & general & \cite{weil1965formule,ichino2007siegel,yamana2011siegel}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Matching} & A statement in the archive's own terms: theta integrals attached to matched data agree up to explicit constants. & internal & ---\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Global\allowbreak{}Euler\allowbreak{}Char} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ over a number field unramified outside $S$: Tate's global Euler characteristic formula. \emph{Tate's formula, for $\ell$-power torsion modules.} & general & \cite{tate1963duality,milne1986arithmetic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Global\allowbreak{}Finiteness} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ as above: $H^0$, $H^1$ and $H^2$ are finite and the higher groups vanish for $\ell\ne2$. \emph{Finiteness of Galois cohomology with restricted ramification.} & general & \cite{tate1963duality,milne1986arithmetic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Euler\allowbreak{}Char} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ at a finite place: Tate's local Euler characteristic formula. \emph{Tate's local formula.} & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Finiteness} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ at a finite place: $H^0$, $H^1$ and $H^2$ are finite and the higher groups vanish. \emph{Finiteness of local Galois cohomology.} & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Tate\allowbreak{}Duality} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ at a finite place: Tate local duality. \emph{Tate local duality.} & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Greenberg\allowbreak{}Wiles} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ and local conditions: the formula of Greenberg and Wiles comparing a Selmer group with the dual Selmer group. \emph{The formula of Greenberg and Wiles.} & general & \cite{wiles1995modular,darmon1995fermat}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Unramified\allowbreak{}Orthogonality} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ at a place not above $\ell$ where $M$ is unramified: the unramified classes of $M$ and of its Tate dual are exact annihilators. \emph{Unramified classes are exact annihilators.} & general & \cite{serre1964cohomologie,milne1986arithmetic,tate1963duality}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Weil\allowbreak{}Unitary\allowbreak{}Convergent} & For a non-degenerate Hermitian form of rank $M$ over a CM extension: $[\U(J)]$ has finite volume, and for $2n<M$ the mean of the theta series of frames with a given Gram matrix is the product of the local densities. \emph{Finite volume, and the formula in Weil's range as a mass formula for representation densities.} & general & \cite{siegel1935analytische,braun1941theorie,weil1965formule,borel1962arithmetic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Euler\allowbreak{}Char\allowbreak{}K} & For $K/\Q_\ell$ finite and a finite continuous $\ell^r$-torsion module: $\#H^1=\#H^0\cdot\#H^2\cdot\#M^{[K:\Q_\ell]}$. \emph{Tate's local formula for finite extensions of $\Q_\ell$.} & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Finiteness\allowbreak{}K} & For $K/\Q_\ell$ finite and such a module: $H^0$, $H^1$, $H^2$ are finite and $H^n=0$ for $n\ge3$. \emph{Finiteness for finite extensions of $\Q_\ell$.} & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Tate\allowbreak{}Duality\allowbreak{}K} & For $K/\Q_\ell$ finite: $H^2(G_K,\mu_{\ell^r})\cong\Z/\ell^r$ and the cup-product pairings with the Tate dual are perfect. \emph{Tate local duality for finite extensions of $\Q_\ell$.} & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Every\allowbreak{}Character} & The conclusion: $L(s,\chi)\ne0$ for every Dirichlet character $\chi$ and every $s$ with $\re s>\tfrac12$, $s=1$ excluded for trivial $\chi$. The file returns it under the hypothesis of \cref{st:vwin}. & conclusion & ---\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\end{longtable}}
